bugs: Empty query params on the index (`?status=&tag=&per_page=`, which plain HTML forms send) return 422. The rules in app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:14-16 have `sometimes` but no `nullable`, so after ConvertEmptyStringsToNull the null values fail the enum, string and integer rules.
Tag::firstOrCreate in app/Models/Post.php:55 is check-then-insert. Two concurrent requests creating the same new tag can hit the unique index on tags.name and return a 500. createOrFirst avoids this.
antipatterns: app/Http/Requests/IndexPostRequest.php:22: `PostStatus::tryFrom((string) $this->validated('status'))` casts and silently tries again on a value that has already been validated. Using `$this->enum('status', PostStatus::class)` or `from` would say what it means.

app/Models/Post.php:61-70: the scopes accept nullable arguments and wrap themselves in `when()`. This hides the conditional inside the model, so `withStatus(null)` quietly does nothing. The controller is the clearer place for the conditional.
routes/api.php:6-11: four routes declared by hand with prefix and controller grouping, where `Route::apiResource(...)->only(...)` is the conventional form.
app/Models/Post.php:24-26 and the migration default both set the draft default, and the model uses the string literal 'draft' instead of the enum value.
strengths: Thin controller. The query helpers on the FormRequest (`status()`, `tag()`, `perPage()`) keep the index action readable.
Modern Laravel 12 style: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope] attributes, a backed enum cast, Rule::enum, and route `->can()` with separate update and delete policy abilities.
Ownership is enforced at the route through policy middleware, so a non-author gets 403 before validation runs, and there is a test for that.

A rich test suite (30 tests) using hasAttached, freezeSecond and sole. It covers the slug fallback, mass-assignment protection of published_at, tag whitespace trimming and dedupe, clearing tags with an empty array, a tag filter that must not leak other users' posts, the default page size, and per_page bounds.

antipatterns: routes/api.php:7-8: apiResource is registered twice to attach `can:update,post` to update and destroy. Destroy is therefore gated by the `update` ability, which leaves PostPolicy::delete effectively unused (it only delegates to update). `->can()` on a single route, or authorizing in the controller, would be clearer.
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:20: `PostStatus::from($status)` re-parses input that has already been validated. `$request->enum('status', PostStatus::class)` is the idiomatic accessor.
app/Http/Controllers/PostController.php:41: `$request->has('tags')` checks raw input rather than validated data. It works, but `$request->safe()->has('tags')` would be more consistent.
app/Models/Post.php:24-26: the draft default is the string literal 'draft' and duplicates the default in the migration.
strengths: Thin controller with conditional `when()` filters in the controller and clean #[Scope] methods that take typed enum and string arguments.
Index validation uses `nullable`, so empty query params mean no filter, and a test covers that. Per-page is bounded, and withQueryString keeps filters in the pagination links.
Tags are created with createOrFirst, which is safe under concurrent inserts on the unique name column. Names are trimmed, filtered and deduped in a tidy collection pipeline.

Modern Laravel 12 style: #[Fillable], #[ObservedBy], #[Scope], an enum cast, Rule::enum, a composite index on (user_id, status, created_at), and a pivot table with a composite primary key and cascading deletes.
The observer handles the unique slug, with a fallback for titles that produce an empty slug, and sets published_at on save only when it is missing.

Solid tests: guests get 401 on every endpoint, including a non-JSON request; re-publishing after going back to draft keeps the original published_at; a non-author gets 403 even with an invalid body; empty filters; query validation messages.

v.rationale:
The two implementations are nearly identical in structure: an enum cast, an observer for the slug and published_at, a policy, FormRequests, a JsonResource that plucks tag names, a syncTagNames collection pipeline, and modern model attributes. Both suites pass (impl-2: 25 tests, impl-1: 30 tests).

The ranking comes down to small correctness differences found by probing:
- impl-1 returns 422 for empty filter params (`?status=&tag=&per_page=`) because its index rules have no `nullable`. impl-2 handles this and tests it.
- impl-1 uses firstOrCreate for tags, which can race against the unique index. impl-2 uses createOrFirst.

impl-1 has the broader, slightly more idiomatic test suite (hasAttached, freezeSecond, a tag filter leak test, the slug fallback) and separate route-level `can` abilities for update and delete. impl-2's double apiResource registration, with destroy gated by `update`, is a style blemish but not a bug.

Other probes behaved the same in both: a guest's non-JSON request gets 401, a null title or null tags returns 422, nested and whitespace-only tags return 422, array-valued filters return 422, and PATCH works. Neither exposes a show route, which the task didn't ask for.

Because real bugs weigh heavily, impl-2 ranks first.
